core.title: Raise convention gaps and misfires as evidence-backed proposals through the governed path
core.given: An agent in any profile meets a situation no active convention covers, or an active convention that misfires
core.when: it encounters that gap or misfire (including a gap measured in an experiment)
core.then: Record a convention proposal — situation, concrete evidence, proposed rule, target `<profile>.<area>` — where the coach collects proposals for the work.
prefer: First check whether an existing convention covers it; point to it instead of proposing.

Evidence = an observed failure a reader can check: failed/returned review, missed trap or acceptance, same mistake repeated across tasks or agents, a convention that fired where it does not apply or stayed silent where it should, or a measured experiment gap (attach run evidence).
Profile ∈ planner, tester, coder, reviewer, coach, shared (shared only if every profile must receive it). For a change, name the convention id and quote the misfiring part.
Continue the assigned task under the conventions active now.

Coach: collect proposals, merge duplicates. Author: draft in convention format; independent auditor checks. Owner: approve or decline. Approved → new convention in its profile family; declined → recorded as declined with the reason.
avoid: Creating, editing, renaming, disabling or deleting an active convention (anything the catalog currently loads: file, id, relationships, selectors).
Applying the proposed rule to the task that raised it, or treating it as approved before the owner approves.
Proposing from preference, style or hypothetical risk without an observed failure.
Filing without target profile and area.
unless: Exception to avoid[0] only: a task whose explicit, owner-approved purpose is to change the catalog (e.g. a convention rewrite or rename) edits conventions as its deliverable, but still goes through author, auditor and owner review before the change is active.
Reporting that an active convention could not be followed is not a proposal and is always allowed: state the blocker in the report and continue or stop as the other active conventions require.
core.why: Editing an active convention for the current task removes its guard, and preference-driven rules add noise weaker models then follow; one governed, review-only path keeps the catalog small, evidence-backed and owned.
evidence: The task diff contains no change to any active convention's file, id, relationships or selectors, unless the task is an owner-approved catalog task.

Each proposal raised is a durable record where the coach collects proposals for the work, with situation, concrete evidence, proposed rule and target `<profile>.<area>`; change proposals name the existing convention id and quote the misfiring part.

Evidence in the proposal is checkable by a reader (failed/returned review, missed trap or acceptance, repeated mistake, misfiring convention, or measured experiment gap with run evidence); no preference, style or hypothetical-risk-only proposals.
The task's work and verification were done under the conventions active at the time, not under the proposed rule.

Catalog changes (including owner-approved catalog tasks) reach the catalog only after author draft, independent audit and owner approval; proposals were collected by the coach with duplicates merged; declined proposals are recorded as declined with the reason.
verification: No automated detector exists for this rule; review enforces it. An edit to an active convention outside an owner-approved catalog task is a finding.
Only the agent or a reviewer can judge that the catalog has a gap or a misfire; there is nothing to auto-detect for the proposal duty itself.
Whether a task is owner-approved catalog work cannot be read from task terms alone; confirm it from the task's approval record or by review.

A changed file that belongs to the convention catalog (its location is repository configuration) is visible in the changed-file list and signals a possible edit of an active convention, but is not by itself a violation.

Term convention_proposal: a durable record with four parts — situation the agent met, evidence that the current conventions failed there, proposed rule (new, or a change to a named existing convention), target profile and area. It is a request for review, not a rule.

Term concrete_evidence: an observed failure a reader can check — failed or returned review; trap or acceptance the work missed; same mistake repeated across tasks or agents; existing convention that fired where it does not apply or stayed silent where it should apply; measured experiment gap. A preference, style opinion or hypothetical risk is NOT evidence.
Term target_family: the `<profile>.<area>` prefix the proposed rule would take; profile ∈ {planner, tester, coder, reviewer, coach, shared}; shared only when every profile must receive the rule.
Term active_convention: any convention the agent's catalog currently loads, including its file, id, relationships and selectors.

Proposal path checked: (1) agent records proposal (situation, evidence, proposed rule, target profile and area) where the coach collects proposals for the work; (2) coach collects proposals and merges duplicates; (3) an author drafts the rule in the convention format and an independent auditor checks it; (4) owner approves or declines; (5) approved rule is added as a new convention in its profile family; declined proposal is recorded as declined, with the reason.

Enforcement summary: agents suggest new rules or changes to existing rules only as evidence-backed proposals; the coach collects them, an author drafts them in the convention format, an auditor checks them, and only the owner can approve one into the catalog. The catalog changes only through review.

fires: An agent in any profile meets a situation no active convention covers.
An active convention fires on work it does not apply to, or stays silent where it should apply.
An experiment measures a gap (e.g. a hard task where conventions did not close the gap to a stronger model).
An agent's diff touches an active convention's file, id, relationships or selectors.
An owner-approved catalog task edits conventions as its deliverable: the edit is allowed, but the change must still pass author, auditor and owner review before it is active.
The coach, an author, an auditor or the owner handles collected convention proposals.
doesNotFire: The situation is already covered by an existing active convention that fired correctly (point to it; no proposal).
The agent only reports that an active convention could not be followed in the current task and states the blocker; that report is not a proposal.

bunOnly.reason: The ATDD-Bun sidecar's checker-implementation declaration (implementation.type none) is realization configuration of that stack's checker; the neutral core states generically that no automated detector exists and review enforces the rule.

bunOnly.text: path_glob fact with the value `<convention catalog directory>/**`
bunOnly.reason: The path-glob expression locating the convention catalog, and the sidecar's 'path_glob' fact kind, have no stack-neutral equivalent: a neutral core names no path. The core keeps the same signal role-neutrally — a changed file belongs to the convention catalog, whose location is repository configuration, observable in the changed-file list and only a signal, not by itself a violation. The exact glob stays with the realization (bun.json itself is the delivered reference example).

neutralityNotes: This rule governs the ATDD convention system itself and is already stack-neutral: the ATDD governance roles (coach, author, auditor, owner) and profile families (planner, tester, coder, reviewer, coach, shared) are framework concepts, not stack specifics, and are kept in the core. The core therefore needs nothing from the structure profile: profileRequirements and proposedKeys are empty. Three things could not be carried one-to-one. (1) bun.json's activation fact kind 'path_glob' has no counterpart in the neutral activation vocabulary (role|operation|change|phase|finding|file_kind|task_term|task_has_acceptance), and a neutral core may not embed a path expression; the core states the same signal role-neutrally as an observable 'change' fact — a changed file belongs to the convention catalog, whose location is repository configuration, visible in the changed-file list and only a signal of a possible edit, not by itself a violation — while the glob form `<convention catalog directory>/**` stays with the realization (bunOnly; bun.json itself is delivered as the reference example). (2) The activation facts' 'note' fields are not representable in the neutral facts shape (fact/values/observability only); their operative content — no detector exists and review enforces, owner-approval of catalog work is confirmed from the task's approval record or by review, and a change belonging to the catalog location is a signal rather than by itself a violation — is preserved in core:verification. (3) The ATDD-Bun checker's '(implementation.type none)' declaration is realization detail (bunOnly); the core states generically that no automated detector exists and review enforces the rule. Per-rule severity and disposition (Severity 3; strict) stay with the rule in core:verification, not in the profile.
